---
title: "Use packs"
---

A pack is a named, versioned collection of hooks you enable instead of copying
hook files into your repo. Builtin packs ship inside `capt-hook`; external packs
live in a GitHub repo; plugin packs ride in on enabled Claude Code plugins. You
list the packs you want as `[packs.<name>]` tables in `.claude/capt-hook.toml`,
and the loader imports them alongside your own `.claude/hooks/` modules.

## Enable a builtin pack

`capt-hook` ships five builtin packs: `general` (language-agnostic guards for git/jj
safety, code stewardship, task and plan discipline, a review gate, a
docs-freshness gate that blocks a stop once when the session's diff changed
user-facing behavior that README.md or `docs/` don't reflect, a
tombstone-comment nudge that flags a comment narrating the edit itself, such
as `# removed the retry logic`, before it lands, and an LLM-judged detour
nudge that catches side work nobody asked for and tells the agent to check in
with 2-4 options instead of improvising), `python`
(a pytest-before-commit gate, AST style rules, and a `uv` missing-dependency nudge),
`go` (a go-test-before-commit gate and a `go.mod` nudge on module-resolution
errors), `steering` (four judgment hooks — it flags a plan-mode plan that
band-aids the symptom instead of fixing the root cause, pushes back when you dismiss
a real pre-existing issue, stops the chase after trivial type-checker noise, and
blocks a turn-end that swaps the requested fix for docs or a follow-up the user
never asked for),
and `fixes` (workarounds for upstream Claude Code issues, one hook that
auto-approves a teammate's Bash permission dialogs when the process tree shows the
session was launched with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, and a second that
auto-approves file-tool writes whose target resolves into a temp or scratch
directory under the same launch flag, so bypass-consented sessions stop popping
dialogs for heredocs, redirects, and plan-phase scratch files).
Add one by name:

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack add general
```

This records the pack in `.claude/capt-hook.toml`:

```toml
[packs.general]
```

That entry is the whole change — `pack add` edits `.claude/capt-hook.toml` and nothing else,
since the captain-hook plugin already registers every event. The pack's hooks fire
on the next event. Verify them with the inline tests every hook carries:

```bash
uvx capt-hook test
```

## List, update, and remove packs

List the enabled packs — kind, source ref, version, and hook count:

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack list
```

```
  general                  builtin  -                    v0.19.0  11 hooks
  python                   builtin  -                    v0.1.0   3 hooks
  go                       builtin  -                    v0.1.0   2 hooks
  steering                 builtin  -                    v0.7.0   2 hooks
  fixes                    builtin  -                    v0.2.0   2 hooks
  acme-guards              github   latest@a1b2c3d       v1.4.0   4 hooks
  acme-notes               plugin   acme-notes@acme      v0.3.0   3 hooks
```

Builtin and pinned packs show their manifest `version`. A moving pack —
`@latest` or a bare default-branch source — shows the ref it last resolved to
instead: the release tag here, or the branch name for a bare source. That ref
lives in the pack's per-machine sidecar, so a machine that has never resolved
the pack falls back to the manifest version until its first `pack update`. A
`plugin` row is a pack discovered on an enabled Claude Code plugin — its ref is
the plugin id, and no config entry exists for it; see
[Ship a pack in a Claude plugin](plugin-packs.qmd).

Remove a pack by name. The entry leaves `.claude/capt-hook.toml`, but its cache
stays on disk for other projects:

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack remove general
```

## Add a pack from GitHub

Point `pack add` at a GitHub repo as `github:owner/repo@ref`, where `ref` is a
tag, branch, or commit (omit it to track the default branch):

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack add github:acme/guards@v1.2
```

`pack add` resolves the ref to a commit, downloads that commit as a tarball into
`~/.cache/captain-hook/packs/`, validates its manifest, and pins the commit in
`.claude/capt-hook.toml`:

```toml
[packs.acme-guards]
source = "github:acme/guards@v1.2"
commit = "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0"
```

The pinned `commit` makes hydration reproducible: a teammate who clones the repo
gets the exact same commit even if the tag later moves — the first event
auto-fetches an uncached pack, so hydration needs no manual step. A cached pack
never touches the network; only a pack that is both uncached and unreachable
fails, with a one-line stderr notice telling you to run `pack update` when back
online.

Re-resolve a tracked ref to its latest commit and re-fetch:

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack update acme-guards
```

Run `pack update` with no name to refresh every external pack.

## The hook command

Hook commands are plugin-owned. The captain-hook plugin's `hooks.json` registers
`uvx --isolated capt-hook run <Event>` for every event, and the string is identical
on every machine, so a fresh clone gets working hooks with nothing installed beyond
`uv`.
Nothing a pack does changes that: `pack add`, `pack remove`, and a pinned
`pack update` edit only the `[packs.*]` tables in `.claude/capt-hook.toml`, a
moving-ref `pack update` only refreshes its per-machine sidecar, and none of
them touch the hook commands. The rewrite is section-scoped, so a coexisting
`[pack]` table and its comments survive byte-for-byte.

## How packs combine with your own hooks

Your `.claude/hooks/` modules import first, so they register ahead of pack hooks.
A block from any hook wins the event outright; among approvals the first
registered wins, so your local approval outranks a pack's on the same event.
Packs are the shared baseline; your local hooks stay authoritative.

Across the pack tiers, the more explicit source wins: local hooks, then
`[packs.*]` entries, then packs discovered on enabled plugins. A `[packs.*]`
entry always shadows a same-name plugin pack — a pinned external gets its exact
commit even when an enabled plugin ships the same pack, a `disabled = true`
entry suppresses it outright, and the shadow holds even while an external is
offline and uncached. See
[Ship a pack in a Claude plugin](plugin-packs.qmd#precedence) for the plugin
tier's own tie-breaks.

## Author a pack

A pack repo needs a `capt-hook.toml` manifest with a `[pack]` table and a
directory of hook `.py` files. The manifest may live at `.claude/capt-hook.toml`,
beside your other Claude Code config, or at the repo root; of the two locations,
the file that actually carries a `[pack]` table wins, so a consumer-only
`.claude` file (just `[packs.*]` enablement, as `pack add` writes) never shadows
a root manifest. The `[pack]` table names the pack,
versions it, and points at the hooks directory:

```toml
[pack]
name = "acme-guards"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Guards for ACME service conventions"
hooks = "hooks"
```

`name`, `description`, and `hooks` are required; `version` defaults to `0.0.0`
(a pack consumed `@latest` shows its resolved release tag in `pack list`
anyway), `nlp = true` declares the [spaCy
resources](troubleshooting.qmd#nlpsignal-hooks-need-the-spacy-model), and
`marketplaces` lists [extra dependency
marketplaces](plugin-packs.qmd#extra-dependency-marketplaces). A directory is a
pack if and only if its manifest has a `[pack]` table, and every malformed
manifest raises `PackError` — a missing required key fails loud, at load time.

The two config axes share one file format on purpose: `[pack]` makes a
directory a pack, `[packs.*]` tables enable packs for a project, and a single
`.claude/capt-hook.toml` can carry both — a pack repo that also consumes other
packs is one file, not two. `pack add` and `pack remove` rewrite only the
`[packs.*]` tables, so a coexisting `[pack]` table and its comments are safe — a
rewrite that would alter the `[pack]` table raises `PackError` and leaves the
file untouched.

The `hooks` path is relative to the repo root regardless of where the manifest
sits, so moving the manifest into `.claude/` needs no other change. Set
`hooks = "."` when the hook files sit beside the manifest. Each hook file is a
flat module that imports from `captain_hook` and registers with the same
primitives you use locally:

```python
from captain_hook import Allow, Block, Input, block_command

block_command(
    ["git", "push", "--force"],
    reason="Force-push rewrites shared history",
    hint="Push a new commit instead",
    tests={
        Input(command="git push --force"): Block(),
        Input(command="git push"): Allow(),
    },
)
```

The `name` in the manifest becomes the consumer's `[packs.<name>]` key, so it
must be a slug matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`. Tag a release, and consumers add the
pack with `uvx capt-hook pack add github:acme/guards@v1.2`.

Shipping the pack inside a Claude plugin instead takes two more artifacts on
top of the manifest. `uvx capt-hook pack scaffold .` writes all three and lints
the result — see [Ship a pack in a Claude plugin](plugin-packs.qmd).

## Migrate from 9.x

The 9.x enable-list lived at `.claude/hooks/packs.toml`; 10.x reads
`.claude/capt-hook.toml` and never touches the legacy path — no warning, no
fallback. The entry grammar is unchanged, so a consumer repo migrates with one
move:

```bash
git mv .claude/hooks/packs.toml .claude/capt-hook.toml
```

A pack-source repo additionally wraps its manifest keys under a `[pack]` header.
Both leniencies that make staging safe are deliberate: 9.x ignores unknown
top-level tables and never reads the new consumer path, so a repo can carry the
new file (or a dual-grammar manifest) before upgrading and delete the old one
after.

::: {.callout-warning title="An unmigrated repo loads zero packs, silently"}
Under 10.x, a repo whose enable-list still sits at `.claude/hooks/packs.toml`
dispatches with no packs at all and no error. `uvx capt-hook pack list` shows
the empty roster, and `uvx capt-hook heartbeats --session <id>` confirms events
still arrive.
:::
